title: feat(plugin-auth): a forced password change requires a password different from the current one
body:
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:管理员要求"下次登录必须改密码"的用户,在完成这次强制改密时,新密码必须与当前(管理员发的临时)密码不同;`/change-password` 与 `/reset-password` 两个能清除该标记的入口都会拒绝相同密码(400 `PASSWORD_REUSE`),控制台强制改密页用用户语言提示同一句话。
- 为什么改:强制改密的目的就是让用户离开管理员知道的密码;现在由服务端直接保证这一点,不再取决于 `passwordHistoryCount` 的设置。
- 风险与回滚:只影响强制改密标记仍在的用户;未带标记的改密行为与 history 设置不变。每次改密多一次 `sys_user` 读。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-password-session-policy.ts`(`assertPasswordNotReused` 新增的 forced 分支,尤其"先验当前密码再判新密码"那段)、`auth-manager-before-hook.ts`(传入 currentPassword 的那几行)、`ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/RemediationOverlay.tsx`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/forced-password-change-new-password.test.ts`,预期 5/5 通过。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- **plugin-auth.** While an administrator's forced password change (`sys_user.must_change_password`) is outstanding, `assertPasswordNotReused` refuses a new password that verifies against the CURRENT hash with `400 PASSWORD_REUSE` and the message "Choose a new password that is different from your temporary password.", whatever `passwordHistoryCount` is (the default 0 included). The flag is cleared only by `stampPasswordChangedAt`, which the after-hook runs on a successful `/change-password` or `/reset-password`; both doors pass through this check in the before-hook first, so every user-facing door that clears the flag is covered. Sign-up (a new user) and the administrator's own Set Password with the requirement switched off are the other writers of the flag and are not user completion doors.
- **The refusal answers only a caller who proved the current password.** On `/change-password` better-auth verifies `currentPassword` only after the before-hook, so the new branch first verifies the request's `currentPassword` against the current hash and judges the new password only when that holds; a wrong current password is left to the endpoint's own `INVALID_PASSWORD`. `/reset-password` carries no such claim (its token is the authority) and is judged directly.
- **Unchanged:** with no forced change outstanding, reuse is judged by `passwordHistoryCount` exactly as before (depth 0 still accepts the same password; the one extra cost is a `sys_user` flag read per change/reset). The code is the existing `PASSWORD_REUSE` (the condition is reuse of the current password), so the error-code ledger and `packages/spec` do not move.
- **Console.** The forced-reset screen (`PASSWORD_RESET_REQUIRED`) shows `auth.remediation.password.sameAsTemporary` in the user's language when the new password equals the one typed as current, and sends no request. The key is added to all ten locale packs (the key-parity test requires it). An expiry (`PASSWORD_EXPIRED`) screen is unchanged; the server judges reuse there.
- `.changeset/forced-password-change-new-password.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n` patch.

## Tests

- New `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/forced-password-change-new-password.test.ts`, end to end through `AuthManager.handleRequest` over a real `ObjectQL` engine (better-sqlite3, the plugin's own manifest, so the `internal: true` strip of `sys_account.password` is live): refused on `/change-password` with the flag set (status, code, message; flag still set; current password still signs in); a different password completes and clears the flag; a wrong current-password claim gets `INVALID_PASSWORD`, not `PASSWORD_REUSE`; `/reset-password` refused then completed; control: no flag + depth 0 still accepts the same password.
- `auth-manager.test.ts`: the depth-0 no-op case now pins that only the `sys_user` flag is read and `sys_account` is not.
- New `ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/RemediationOverlay.forcedResetNewPassword.test.tsx`: en and zh text shown and no request sent; a different password is sent; an expiry screen sends the same password on.

## Acceptance notes

- The flag read fails open (treated as not set) on a lookup error, as every read in `assertPasswordNotReused` already does.
- The Console check compares the two typed strings; it never replaces the server's refusal, which stays the authority for every client.
